messages:
jess (support): FYI got a high-priority escalation from Acme. Customers seeing p95/p99 spikes on text-generation endpoints since 11:10 UTC. They reported 2x-3x latency and occasional 503s.

alex (eng-runtime): Thanks Jess. Any quick signal which region/model?

jess (support): Mostly us-west1, model=gpt-small-quant, trend aligns with last rollout at 10:55. They attached a trace showing >500ms token delays.

priya (eng-runtime): Pulling metrics now. Early look: prefix_cache_miss_rate jumped ~6x at ~10:57, eviction_rate up too. p95 tokens/sec drops when misses spike.

sam (oncall): @priya can you paste the query you ran? I want to correlate with autoscale events.

priya (eng-runtime): Prometheus: 
```
sum by(prefix) (rate(prefix_cache_miss_total[2m]))
```
and
```
sum(rate(prefix_cache_eviction_total[2m]))
```
Shows hotset for prefixes starting with "user:acme/" and many single-use prefixes.

marta (infra): Interesting — autoscaler didn't fire, capacity healthy. So it's not load, it's efficiency per-GPU down. Could be cache key explosion -> cold KV fills.

alex (eng-runtime): Any recent changes to key normalization or user-provided prefixes? We released the normalization tweak in the deploy at 10:50.

priya (eng-runtime): Yes — the normalization PR (strip-extra-suffix) landed. Hypothesis: normalization made keys more unique for some inputs (e.g., stripping caused collisions to become distinct because trailing contexts were preserved), increasing cardinality.

jess (support): Customer said they started sending structured metadata in prompts yesterday, might interact with key logic.

sam (oncall): Repro steps requested. Jess, can you ask for a minimal request body that reproduces elevated miss rate? If not, we'll try fuzzing with their anonymized prefix examples.

jess (support): Asked and they provided anonymized example: 
```
{"prompt": "<user_prompt>", "meta": {"session_id": "abc-123-xyz-987", "client_ctx": "flow:checkout:step:3"}}
```
They say session_id changes every request.

alex (eng-runtime): That session_id being embedded into prefix key will absolutely increase cardinality. We should not include ephemeral session ids in cache key.

priya (eng-runtime): Confirmed. Current key pattern: `prefix:${user_id}:${session_id}:${trunc(prompt,50)}`. The normalization change moved `session_id` position and made truncation behave differently. Result: many unique keys, tiny hotset per key, thrash.

sam (oncall): Quick mitigation options?

marta (infra): Short-term: route Acme traffic to a warmed pool where we prepopulate common prefixes (if we can derive them) or temporarily increase prefix cache size per-pod and bump memory reservation. Longer-term: change key composition and add TTL-based aggregation.

alex (eng-runtime): I can push a hotfix to key generation to skip session_id if it matches UUID regex. Small patch, deploy as a canary to one pod pool.

priya (eng-runtime): Also recommend enabling prefix-cache-prefetch for that customer (warmup using recent prefixes list) and lowering eviction aggressiveness from 0.7 to 0.85 (soft cap) so we don't thrash on sudden cardinality.

jess (support): Customer asked for ETA. Can we try the skip-session-id hotfix now and monitor?

sam (oncall): I'll coordinate. Steps: 1) rollback normalization PR flag (feature flag) OR apply hotfix to key gen, 2) increase prefix cache size by 20% for us-west1 cluster, 3) enable verbose cache metrics for that tenant, 4) monitor p95/p99 and prefix_miss_rate.

alex (eng-runtime): Working on a quick patch. Diff: 
```diff
- key = f"prefix:{user}:{session}:{trunc(prompt,50)}"
+ if session and UUID_REGEX.match(session):
+   key = f"prefix:{user}:{trunc(prompt,50)}"
+ else:
+   key = f"prefix:{user}:{session}:{trunc(prompt,50)}"
```
Deploying to canary pool now.

marta (infra): Increasing cache size on us-west1 group-7 by +25% now (temporary).

ops-bot: Deploy started: alex/key-hotfix -> canary-pool-7 (deployer:alex)

priya (eng-runtime): After canary, initial telemetry looks better: prefix_miss_rate down ~60% on canary pods, p95 token latency improved by ~120ms.

sam (oncall): Great. If canary holds for 15m, roll to remainder of us-west1. Also create an SLO guard to temporarily divert new sessions to larger cache tier if miss rate > X.

jess (support): Customer confirmed noticeable improvement. They're happy for now but want a postmortem and permanent fix.

alex (eng-runtime): I'll open a postmortem ticket and include root cause: key normalization + ephemeral session id in key -> cache cardinality explosion -> eviction thrash -> p95/p99 regressions. Planned permanent fix: 1) key composition policy (drop ephemeral ids), 2) add unit tests for key entropy, 3) TTL-based eviction for tiny hot keys, 4) add tenant-specific prewarming hooks.

priya (eng-runtime): Also adding a regression alert: if prefix_miss_rate increases >3x without corresponding QPS increase, alert paging to eng-runtime.

marta (infra): Filing infra task to limit per-tenant cache growth and offer a soft quota to avoid memory overcommit.

sam (oncall): Closing loop — will monitor next 2 hours. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

jess (support): Thanks everyone — passing update to Acme.
